To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the composition and distribution of the planktonic assemblages of coccolithoprids, diatoms, dinoflagelletes and radiolarians is related to surface water mass distribution; the composition and distribution patterns of the plankton assemblages are preserved in the sediment record; the preservation of the sedimentary record allows the distinction of four ecostratigraphy units in the late Weichelsian and Holocene.

the planktonic microfossil record in the Norwegian-Grenland Sea is a relict of the former living communities and that the composition of the sediment assemblages is related to the distribution of water masses.
the distribution of living coccolithophore communities and their flux to the seafloor is related to surface water mass properties.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the reconstruction of the palaeoecological development of the planktic communities in the Norwegian-Greeland Sea during the last 15 ka BP.
the development and application of a method to reconstruct the plankton community and its environment during the late Quaternar
the development of plankton communities and their preservation in the Norwegian-Greeland Sea.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the sedimentary record of planktonic microorganisms in the Norwegian-Grenland Sea is a valuable tool for palaeo-oceonographic reconstructions.
the sedimentary record of plankton groups is an actualistic and reliable tool for reconstructing palaeoceanography.
the actualistic approach is an effective tool to reconstruct the history of plankton communities.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the actualistic approach provides a powerful tool for the interpretation of the fossil record.
the planktonic fossil records are useful indicators of the palaeo-oceangraphic history of the Norwegian-Green Sea.
the planktonic assemblages are well suited as palaeo-oecological indicators in this region.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the composition of living plankton communities is closely related to the distribution of the water masses.
the distribution of living communities is a good proxy for the distribution of fossil assemblages.
actualistic studies are a valuable tool to understand the development of plankton communities and their fossil record.
